_note: Game-wide configuration — everything that is not specific to the run's content. The run itself lives in content/dongho/level.json. Run ../tools/validate_data.py to check.
_difficultyNote: TWO AXES, DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT JOBS. Difficulty ACROSS CHAPTERS is PROGRESSION — it comes from the shape of the problem and the danger profile (floors -> the trap era -> ceilings), never from harsher numbers, and BRIEF-05 §3 requires it. Difficulty INSIDE the run is ACCOMMODATION — the player-facing Dễ/Thường/Khó control, and it changes ONLY HOW MUCH THE GAME TELLS YOU AND HOW MUCH SLACK IT LEAVES. It never touches a starting stat, a choice cost, a flag or the victory rule. Hard mode is not a bigger bill; it is playing without hindsight. That distinction is the whole point: if difficulty scaled the numbers, a Khó victory and a Dễ victory would mean different things, the leaderboard would be meaningless, and the level's argument — that the historical path is affordable but only just — would be a different argument at every setting.

_neverChangesRationale.omens: Omens announce what was coming, and the households genuinely knew — war reached the district, offset calendars were already in the shops, the survey team was announced. Suppressing them at a higher difficulty would not be difficulty, it would be a false claim about what was knowable at the time.
_neverChangesRationale.runReview: The run review is where a defeat becomes a lesson, which is the entire educational payload. Gating it behind a difficulty would hand the teaching to exactly the players who needed it least.
_neverChangesRationale.minigameCompletion: A minigame is the ritual of a carrier flag, never an extra gate. If dexterity could permanently fail a flag, difficulty would change outcomes — which mayNotChange forbids. Khó strips hints; it never strips completion.

difficultyPolicy._invariantRationale: Every dial in mayChange is information or slack. Every item in mayNotChange is either a historical claim or part of the level's argument. The linter checks that no difficulty entry declares a key outside mayChange — the list is the enforcement, not a comment.
difficultyPolicy._weaveNote: Difficulty deliberately does NOT bias the weave draw. The solvency invariant in weavePolicy is proved against a uniform draw; letting Khó deal a hostile hand would either break that proof or require re-deriving it per difficulty. Hard mode withholds help. It does not stack the deck.

blurb.vi: Nghề chỉ đường. Sổ gia truyền mở sẵn từ đầu, và người nhà báo động sớm.
blurb.en: The craft points the way. The ledger is open from the first card, and the household warns you early.

blurb.vi: Nghề chỉ lúc, không chỉ đường. Sổ gia truyền mở ra khi giữ chắc được điều đầu tiên.
blurb.en: The craft tells you when, not what. The ledger opens once you have secured your first preparation.

blurb.vi: Không ai mách nước, không sổ gia truyền, không đường lui. Người làng năm ấy cũng không có.
blurb.en: No advisors, no ledger, no way back from the edge. The households of those years had none either.

difficulties.minigameHints: icons only, no labels, no reference image

_difficultyDesignNotes.kho: crisisBands: null means a stat touching 0 or 100 ends the run on the spot, with no rescue. That is the correct shape for the top difficulty: the households of those years had no safety net either.
_difficultyDesignNotes.ledgerDisclosure: The three settings are the three answers to 'how much hindsight does the player get'. from-start names the preparations; after-first-flag reveals the shape once the player has secured one, keeping the when-not-what hint policy; at-final-trial means the player finds out what was required at the moment it is judged, which is what the households themselves experienced.
